material.text_fr: Dans le tiroir d'Odile, un Polaroid : un port, des bateaux, et « 1971 » au dos.
Vous avez promis à M. Marchand de retrouver le peintre « L. » avant son anniversaire.
Aider Margaux à refaire la carte du Mistral avant le printemps.
L'avenir du Mistral : le garder, le changer, ou le laisser partir ?
Gus a reçu une lettre d'un notaire, avec un timbre étranger, et il ne l'ouvre pas.
Romy vous a demandé d'être la voix française de son documentaire radio.
Lila et Berlin : peut-on vouloir quelqu'un ici, et vouloir son départ pour elle ?
Qui était Odile, et pourquoi est-elle partie ?
Rue de Lancry, au troisième, une fenêtre est encore allumée.

departed.name: Lila Bonnet
departed.why: Lila left for Berlin on 8 January (T8, the platform) and lives there now.

rules: The whole cast knows the learner: never a stranger's welcome, never the vous of strangers from the group.
The continuation may look for «L.», ask about the rue de Lancry, follow the painting; it never reveals who L. is — that answer belongs to the next authored season.
facts: The learner kept Odile's flat above Le Mistral and lives there now.
Le Mistral is exactly as it was; Margaux runs it alone, on a nine-year lease.
M. Marchand left the building for a residence without stairs; Solvel owns his floors, he kept the café's walls.
Only four people know Odile's notebook page; Gus knows nothing of it.
The painting «Le Mistral sur le canal» is with the learner; its back reads «Pour Odile, qui part. — L., 1970» and «Toujours rue de Lancry. — L., 2021».
Marin has put his co-op folder in a drawer.
Lila left for Berlin on 8 January; she lives there now. She writes; she is never in a Paris scene.
Odile's last letter has been read: she left two things in Paris, the flat and someone; for the other, «regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral».
Camille Marchand has met the learner and still says vous; the switch to tu belongs to a later season.
The café question of season 1 is closed. Do not reopen it.
M. Marchand comes to Sunday lunch at the learner's, by the 46 bus, as he did at Odile's.
Romy gave the learner the memory card with Margaux's admission, without a word.

draft.logline: After promising M. Marchand to find the painter "L.", you travel to Marseille with Romy and Marin following a Polaroid of a 1971 port; there you record, question, and pry at small truths — and learn how Odile's past shaped the person who left you her flat.
draft.logline_fr: Vous allez à Marseille pour chercher le peintre « L. » et suivre un polaroïd de 1971.
draft.your_arc: You keep your promise and learn to choose between a tidy answer and the messy truth about someone you loved.
draft.first_episode_seed: Romy shows you the Polaroid and plays the voice memo: Margaux's name, a year, a port; you call M. Marchand to say you are going. By evening you have two train tickets and Marin's reluctant backpack.

stages.summary: You leave Paris with Marin and Romy to keep your promise to M. Marchand and follow the Polaroid's hint toward the old port; Antoine meets you and gives the first local names.
Local stories contradict each other: people argue whether Odile was a visitor, a worker, or a lover of the port, and a key address is now a boarded painter's house.
A witness at the fish market describes a woman matching Odile and mentions a small gallery where she left a sketchbook — a concrete clue that points you onward.
Romy asks you to be the French voice for her documentary and begins interviews at the Vieux-Port while you transcribe, translate and ask questions.
An interview subject claims Odile used another name and a recording goes missing from the café, threatening the documentary's honest arc.
You lay down a short narrative voiceover that reframes Odile as an active choice-maker; when Romy plays the clip for a local witness, memories shift and new doors open.
Gus's sealed envelope bears a foreign stamp; you travel to Marseille to retrieve it from the local notary's office and to learn why Gus will not open it.
Céline, the notary assistant, reveals the sender's name and an address that contradicts Gus's family story, forcing him to confront a hidden thread.
Gus opens the letter on the harbour edge; its contents reframe part of his identity and, freed, he offers a key recollection that helps your search for L.
You bring 'Le Mistral sur le canal' to Maïté's gallery to compare pigment and handwriting with local works and to test whether the painting's back-note is original.
Experts disagree about the handwriting and some conservation tests suggest a later inscription; you must decide whether to trust the painting's clue toward Rue de Lancry.
A tiny forensic trace — tar and a known marine pigment from a local dock — ties the painting to the port and confirms Odile's presence there, giving you a new direction.

open_threads.text: Find who Odile was in the port town and why she left Paris; this is the central question that drives small interviews and big silences.
Keep your promise to Mr. Marchand: locate the painter 'L.' and get a name before his birthday; the trip must produce at least a lead.

setting.neighborhood: Vieux-Port / Le Panier — old harbour alleys, stairs, faded workshops
setting.tone: windy, investigative, nostalgic — small revelations, warm tensions
setting.situation: You travel to Marseille with Romy and Marin to follow the Polaroid and to keep your promise to M. Marchand; Romy needs your French voice for her radio piece.
setting.situation_fr: Vous allez à Marseille avec Romy et Marin pour suivre le polaroïd et tenir votre promesse.
setting.why: The material branch b:peintre_l is the promise to M. Marchand to find the painter 'L.'; the Polaroid (p:polaroid_port) points to a port town, and Romy asks for your presence on-site for the documentary, so you must go.

places.description: The old, busy harbour where fishermen, tourists and painters cross paths; many of the season's searches, confrontations and small discoveries happen along the quays and fish stalls.
places.brief: Stone quay and low iron bollards; a row of moored small boats with peeling paint; bright awnings of fish stalls; late-afternoon, warm golden light with a steady northern wind.

places.description: A small, salty café near the harbour where locals trade news and memories — a natural place to meet witnesses and to record Romy's interviews.
places.brief: Narrow tiled terrace with chipped mosaics; a battered brass espresso machine behind the counter; a sun-faded awning and glass jars of sardines on a shelf; warm, diffuse morning light.

places.description: A modest gallery / conservator's workshop that keeps small local paintings and offers handwriting and varnish expertise — a place to compare the 'Mistral' painting and test materials.
places.brief: Tall windows with a paint-stained sill; a table with brushes and labelled jars; framed small seascapes stacked against a wall; cool, northern light through dusty glass.

places.description: An old, boarded atelier-house once home to a local painter — its doorway, courtyard and a locked studio become key scene locations as you search for L.'s traces.
places.brief: Blue-green shuttered doorway with a rusted latch; a small inner courtyard with a drying line and clay pots; a worn wooden studio door with a faded nameplate; late-afternoon shadow and salt smell.

places.description: Noisy, bright market on the quay where men and women who have worked the port for decades give eyewitness accounts and where a decisive witness appears.
places.brief: Rows of ice beds and metal trays; scales and hanging slips of paper; splashes of red fish and silver sardines; sharp, high-contrast morning light with wet stone reflections.

new_characters.name: Antoine Delacourt
new_characters.role: Retired dockworker who ekes out a living selling small restored nets and knows the old port families; he recognizes the place in the Polaroid and offers direction — but he remembers names poorly.
new_characters.personality: Direct, salt-sprayed humour, shy about feelings, stubbornly precise about dates when he chooses to be.
new_characters.wants: To be useful and to be remembered by younger locals as someone who kept the harbour's stories.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Short, concrete sentences, uses local Marseille expressions and nicknames, sometimes slips into past-tense stories.

new_characters.name: Céline Martin
new_characters.role: Assistant at a Marseille notary's office who holds the envelope that arrived for Gus and remembers the sender's handwriting and address details.
new_characters.personality: Careful, a little nervy, professional but curious; she has an eye for small handwriting details.
new_characters.wants: To do her job well and to help people find their pasts when paperwork allows.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Polite, measured, uses precise legal words and dates when needed.

new_characters.name: Maïté Roché
new_characters.role: Gallery conservator who can compare paint layers and who once catalogued a small show of port scenes from the 1960s–70s; she offers technical insight into the Mistral painting.
new_characters.personality: Meticulous, quietly amused by amateurs, generous with knowledge when trust is earned.
new_characters.wants: To restore small-known works and to bring local artists to attention without flashy shows.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Precise, uses conservation vocabulary, patient explanations, warms when telling a painting story.

issues: Risk of revealing «L.»: canon rule explicitly says the continuation may look for «L.» but must not reveal who L. is — the season must keep L.'s identity secret. Wording like the arc title "Trouver L." is fine only if the season produces leads without giving a final name; make this constraint explicit in every stage write-up.

Do not reopen the café question: the world canon states the café question of season 1 is closed (Le Mistral remains as it was). The proposal respects this, but writers must avoid scenes that pull the cast back into a debate about keeping/selling the café.

Lila's absence: canon says Lila left for Berlin and is never in Paris scenes. The proposal includes Marin as travelling cast and does not put Lila on stage — keep her off-screen and preserve her Berlin status and correspondence only.

M. Marchand's expectations: the material branch b:peintre_l is a promise to find L. before his birthday. The proposal must avoid resolving the promise by supplying a definitive identification; instead, deliver a credible lead that honours the promise without producing the forbidden final answer.

Maintain relationships/registers: many new locals are written to use 'vous' with the learner (Antoine, Céline, Maïté). The proposal must keep the established rule that the whole cast knows the learner and avoids the stranger's 'vous' only where canon demands tu/shift later (e.g., Camille).

A2 learner-facing French: overall tone and arcs are appropriate, but be careful with specialised conservation/legal vocabulary in Maïté's and Céline's scenes — keep explanations simple, reuse material vocabulary, and provide repetition so A2 learners can follow technical points without confusion.

Continuity of items: the painting's back-note and forensic clues are already canon facts (the painting is with the learner; it references L.). The proposal correctly uses these; ensure no new contradictory facts about who knew Odile, the notebook page, or the painting provenance are introduced (e.g., avoid implying Gus knew about the notebook if canon says he didn't).

Gus's letter handling: material plant says Gus received a sealed foreign-stamped letter he didn't open. The proposal has Gus opening it in Marseille — that's allowed (it's a thread grounded in p:lettre_gus) but ensure the letter's contents do not contradict existing canon facts about Gus's family or the four people who know Odile's notebook page.
